polychoice

Multinomial choice models, the inflated multinomial logit, and tests of the independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA), for R.

Status: version 0.1.0. DESIGN.md in the repository gives the scope, the parameterisation, the fixed definitions of every test, and the verification protocol.

What it does

  • mnl(): multinomial / conditional logit with case-specific covariates (alternative-specific coefficients), alternative-specific covariates (generic coefficients), alternative-specific constants, varying choice sets, frequency weights, offsets, unit fixed effects, and analytic, outer-product (BHHH), robust, cluster-robust, or bootstrap standard errors. Wide (one row per case) and long (one row per case-alternative pair) layouts.
  • imnl(): the baseline-inflated multinomial logit of Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017, PSRM), for any inflated alternative, with a logit or probit split equation; with several inflated alternatives, the parametrized logit captivity model of Swait and Ben-Akiva (1987), which generalizes the dogit of Gaudry and Dagenais (1979); and captivity_test(), score and likelihood-ratio tests of the multinomial logit against captive choosers.
  • nlogit(): two-level nested logit (RU2 / RUM-consistent form, as mlogit and Stata), free or shared inclusive-value parameters.
  • hev(): heteroskedastic extreme value model (alternative-specific scales), with quadrature checked against integrate() for scale ratios up to 1.6e5 and a boundary flag when a scale runs to zero.
  • mnprobit(): multinomial probit with a free covariance of the utility differences (exact bivariate normal for three alternatives, GHK with Halton draws beyond).
  • remnl(): multinomial logit with random alternative-specific intercepts per unit (adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature; at two alternatives it reproduces lme4::glmer).
  • rologit(): rank-ordered (exploded) logit for complete, partial, and tied rankings (exact tie likelihood; reproduces mlogit’s rank-ordered logit), with rank_test() for the stability of preferences across ranking stages.
  • Separation:
    • separation() is an exact check by linear programming (ties as groups).
    • The maximum-likelihood likelihood-ratio tests compare the suprema of the log-likelihoods under separation. boot_lr_test() calibrates them, rank-ordered fits included.
    • firth = TRUE (Firth’s penalty) and prior = coef_prior(...) (normal, Cauchy or t priors, Gelman et al.’s default scaling) give finite estimates in mnl() and rologit(), tied rankings included. They come with profile penalized-likelihood intervals (confint()) and penalized likelihood-ratio tests (term_test(), combine_test(), lr_test(), rank_test()).
  • Fixed-effects panels: unit dummies with the never-chosen rule, and bias_correct = "jackknife" (split-panel jackknife of the slopes with a time-homogeneity gate).
  • Quantities of interest: predict() (observed-alternative, outcome-stage, and regime probabilities), first_difference() (delta-method or simulation intervals), rrr().
  • Fit and comparison: fit_stats(), classification(), lr_test(), vuong(), boot_lr_test() (parametric-bootstrap LR and Vuong tests for restrictions on the boundary, such as the multinomial logit against the inflated multinomial logit), compare_models(); broom, texreg, and modelsummary support.
  • IIA / misspecification tests: hausman_mcfadden() (variance-difference and joint/suest forms, base drop handled by exact re-basing), small_hsiao() (the correct sqrt(1/2)-weighted form, repeatable over splits), fp_tests() (Fok and Paap 2025: composite-likelihood Hausman and GMM overidentification), and the battery iia_tests().
  • Further specification tests: nested_lm_test() (McFadden 1987 score test of IIA against a nested logit), combine_test() (Cramer-Ridder pooling of alternatives), term_test() (joint Wald / LR tests per term), hl_test() (Fagerland-Hosmer-Bofin goodness of fit), and boot_pvalue() (parametric bootstrap calibration of the tests whose null is the fitted model).
  • Simulators: rmnl(), rnlogit(), rhev(), rmnp(), rrologit().
  • Panel tools: mundlak().
  • Data: pa2006 and pres2004, the two applications of Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017); and seven datasets from published replication archives, sanctions (Liou 2024), fluvax (Liu et al. 2024), bes1987 (Glasgow 2001), defection (Oppenheim et al. 2015, as re-analysed by Cook, Niehaus and Zuhlke 2018), bes2010 (Arzheimer and Evans 2012), cabinets (Baeck, Debus and Imre 2026) and afghan_leaders (Bhatia and Monroe 2024). The published fits of the first four are regression tests.
library(polychoice)
data(pres2004)
f <- vote ~ educ + female + black + hispanic + pid7 + bush_values + battleground + south + gmb +
  agegroup + evangelical + evangelical:gmb + catholic + catholic:gmb + other_religion +
  secular + secular:gmb + ideology + mobilization
m0 <- mnl(f, data = pres2004)
m1 <- imnl(vote ~ educ + female + black + hispanic + pid7 + bush_values + battleground + south + gmb +
             agegroup + evangelical + evangelical:gmb + catholic + catholic:gmb + other_religion +
             secular + secular:gmb + ideology + mobilization | educ + agegroup + mobilization + secular,
           data = pres2004)
compare_models(MNL = m0, BIMNL = m1)
vuong(m1, m0)
boot_lr_test(m0, m1, B = 99, cores = 4)   # calibrated (the multinomial logit is the boundary case of the inflated model); slow:
                                          # every replicate refits the inflated model's multistart
iia_tests(m0, seed = 1)

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("bagozzib/polychoice")

Installing from source requires a C++ compiler (Rtools on Windows).

Documentation

Every function has a help page with examples (help(package = "polychoice")), and five vignettes cover the package:

  • vignette("polychoice"): getting started (data layouts, fitting, quantities of interest, model comparison).
  • vignette("iia"): testing IIA and specification, with the definition of each test and its bootstrap calibration.
  • vignette("inflation"): the inflated multinomial logit, its several maxima, captive alternatives, and the tests against the multinomial logit.
  • vignette("beyond"): nested logit, HEV, multinomial probit, random intercepts, and fixed-effects panels.
  • vignette("applications"): seven published analyses reproduced from the bundled data.

The repository also holds DESIGN.md and, under verification/, the Monte Carlo scripts, their run records on the release build, and a ledger of the results the documentation cites.

Questions and bug reports: https://github.com/bagozzib/polychoice/issues.

Citation and licence

citation("polychoice") gives the reference for the package and for the methods it implements. The package is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 (GPL-3).
